subject: Uganda Jinja–Mbulamuti–Kamuli–Bukungu and Jinja City roads financing
editorialRule: Source preservation only. No numbered Signal may be generated from this memo without original editorial framing and review.

documentedFacts.claim: Uganda's finance ministry asked Parliament to authorize borrowing up to €207.77 million from Citi Bank and other financial institutions for a 127 km road and 10 km of Jinja City roads.
documentedFacts.source: Parliament of Uganda CMIS — Ministry of Finance brief

documentedFacts.claim: The signed civil-works contract is €161.77 million with M/S Power China International Group Limited, dated 15 March 2023.
documentedFacts.source: Parliament of Uganda CMIS — Ministry of Finance brief

documentedFacts.claim: The ATIDI-covered facility is €179.26 million: €161.77 million for civil works plus a stated €17.49 million insurance premium, equal to 10.81% of the civil-works contract.
documentedFacts.source: Parliament of Uganda CMIS — Ministry of Finance brief

documentedFacts.claim: The ATIDI-covered facility is presented with a 10-year tenor, three-year grace period, 1.40% arrangement fee, €20,000 annual agency fee, 2.50% margin over a stated 2.55% six-month-average Euribor, 5.05% stated interest rate, and 0.750% commitment fee.
documentedFacts.source: Parliament of Uganda CMIS — Ministry of Finance brief

documentedFacts.claim: A separate €28.51 million commercial facility covers €26.17 million of land acquisition and €2.34 million of construction supervision and design review; it is presented with a six-year tenor, three-year grace period, 1.40% arrangement fee, €10,000 annual agency fee, 4.50% margin over stated Euribor, 7.05% stated interest rate, and 1.25% commitment fee.
documentedFacts.source: Parliament of Uganda CMIS — Ministry of Finance brief

documentedFacts.claim: The ministry's brief reports total public debt of US$34.86 billion, or 52.7% of GDP, at the end of December 2025.
documentedFacts.source: Parliament of Uganda CMIS — Ministry of Finance brief

documentedFacts.claim: The same road has appeared in prior government budgets, including as Project 1810 in the FY2024/25 UNRA vote.
documentedFacts.source: Uganda Ministry of Finance budget portal — UNRA Vote 113

documentedFacts.claim: Reporting in April 2021 described the corridor as a government promise dating to 2001 and said contractor procurement was then still underway.

corroboratingReports.note: Corroborates the proposed borrowing amount and debt-service concern, but does not identify the road, contractor or detailed financing terms.
Corroborates the road scope, PowerChina contract, ATIDI replacement of Sinosure, premium and component amounts.

derivedCalculations.calculation: €207.77 million / 137 km = approximately €1.52 million per km.
derivedCalculations.caveat: This is a headline financing-per-kilometre figure, not a construction unit cost; the numerator includes insurance, land acquisition, supervision and design review.

derivedCalculations.calculation: €161.77 million / 137 km = approximately €1.18 million per km.
derivedCalculations.caveat: This is the signed civil-works contract divided by the combined stated route length; it is not evidence of final outturn cost.

derivedCalculations.calculation: €17.49 million / €207.77 million = approximately 8.42% of total proposed financing.
derivedCalculations.caveat: The official brief separately states that the premium equals 10.81% of the civil-works contract.

unresolvedQuestions: Which institutions besides Citi Bank would be original lenders, and what shares would each hold?
Who is the named insured, beneficiary and guarantor under the ATIDI instrument, and what events trigger or exclude payment?
What is the amortization schedule and total projected debt service under each facility after fees, premium and variable Euribor?
What sovereign guarantees, indemnities, waivers, governing-law provisions and enforcement rights appear in the finance documents?
Have all land, environmental and social authorizations required before first disbursement been completed?
What is the current commencement, mobilization and disbursement status under the PowerChina contract signed in March 2023?
How do prior appropriations for Project 1810 reconcile with the current financing request and work completed to date?
